page.local.evidence: Each mount is a folder mapped to a made-up host name inside the engine; no web server is started and no port is opened. test/e2e/e2e-decisions-window.ps1 opens a real window on a real list this way, 2026-10-06.

page.locked.evidence: A navigation to any address but the start page's own host is cancelled, every frame navigation is cancelled, and a new-window request is marked handled; each is recorded as a refusal. The address rule is tested with no window in surfaces/webview2/test/test-webview2-surface.ps1; the throwaway proof of 2026-10-06 measured a cancelled navigation in a real window.

requests.closed.evidence: The page posts JSON text and is handed JSON text. Every message goes through Invoke-HordeSurfaceRequest of surfaces/Port.ps1, and a message whose source is not the page's own host is refused before that. No host object is added to the page: AddHostObjectToScript is never called (surfaces/webview2/test/test-webview2-surface.ps1 reads the adapter's syntax tree for it).

push.evidence: An event is posted to the page as one line of JSON. test/e2e/e2e-decisions-window.ps1 adds a question while the window is open and the page reports one more row without a reload, 2026-10-06.

window.native.evidence: The surface is a top-level window of this process and hands its handle to the caller. The terminal host's own end-to-end scenario has this window owned by, placed beside and following a terminal window that scenario started, 2026-10-06.
